E1 shows currencyservice latency p50 z=403, the strongest deviation, with frontend p90 following it. E1 also shows currencyservice memory at z=69.8. E2 traces put currencyservice on every worst path, but the path continues to productcatalogservice, so the downstream hop is still a possible source. The fault type is also open: delay vs memory pressure. currencyservice logs should show whether there are OOM/GC or memory errors (pointing to mem) or plain slow responses and timeouts (pointing to delay). E1 (metrics) and E2 (traces) both involve currencyservice, but the worst trace path ends at productcatalogservice. I will check productcatalogservice's own metrics directly before ruling it out. That should also help separate delay from memory pressure: a p50 latency jump of about 2000% is much larger than the memory rise of about 349%.

Two independent telemetry kinds point at currencyservice. E1 metrics show its latency-50 at z=403.46 (2017%), the largest deviation in the system. E2 traces show it on every worst path, at about 4.5-4.8s each. Productcatalogservice is a weak candidate: E4 shows only a modest latency-50 deviation (z=4.38) and its CPU went down, so it does not look like the source of a slowdown this large. Frontend latency-90 (z=156.1) closely matches currencyservice latency-90 (z=156.44), which fits frontend being a symptom. E3 logs are all info-level success lines, so there is no error signature. The open question is the fault type. A latency z of 403 versus a memory z of 69.8 favors injected delay, but a 349% memory increase could also mean a memory fault causing the slowdown. Looking at all of currencyservice's metrics (CPU, memory, latency percentiles) should separate the two: a memory fault would usually show memory as the leading or earliest deviation, possibly with CPU or GC effects, while injected delay would mainly raise latency.
